records.name: Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (Visakhapatnam Steel Plant)
records.state_link: Headquarters and plant in Visakhapatnam
records.administrative: Ministry of Steel
records.financials: April-December 2024: total income Rs 12,615.03 crore; loss before tax Rs 3,943.43 crore. Net worth Rs (-)4,538 crore on 31 March 2024.
records.summary: The state-owned company behind the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, India's only shore-based integrated steel plant in the government sector, with 7.3 million tonnes a year of liquid-steel capacity. With its net worth wiped out and bank loans in default, the Union Cabinet approved a Rs 11,440 crore revival plan in January 2025.
detail: RINL runs the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, which the Ministry of Steel describes as 'the only offshore steel plant under Government sector in the state of Andhra Pradesh', with an installed capacity of 7.3 million tonnes a year of liquid steel. It is a Schedule A CPSE under the Ministry of Steel, 100% owned by the Government of India.

According to the Cabinet's January 2025 release, RINL's 'financial condition is critical': its net worth on 31 March 2024 was Rs (-)4,538 crore, current liabilities of Rs 26,114.92 crore far exceeded current assets of Rs 7,686.24 crore, it had exhausted its bank borrowing limits, and it defaulted on capital-loan repayments and interest in June 2024.

On 17 January 2025 the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a revival plan of Rs 11,440 crore: Rs 10,300 crore of fresh equity and conversion of a Rs 1,140 crore working-capital loan into preference shares, 'to keep RINL as a going concern'. In April to December 2024 RINL reported total income of Rs 12,615.03 crore and a loss before tax of Rs 3,943.43 crore, and total liabilities of about Rs 38,965 crore on 31 December 2024.

sources.supports: Schedule A status, 100% government ownership, capacity, financial condition, the Rs 11,440 crore revival plan
April-December 2024 production, income, loss and liabilities

records.administrative: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
records.summary: The state's industrial landlord: a wholly state-owned company that acquires land, develops industrial parks and allots plots to investors at prices the government sets. In August 2026 the government approved discounted APIIC land and incentives for two data-centre projects near Visakhapatnam.
detail: APIIC was incorporated on 26 September 1973 and is 'a wholly owned Undertaking of Government of Andhra Pradesh', with a paid-up capital of Rs 16.33 crore, according to its own website. It says it has developed more than 300 industrial parks and allots land and sheds to entrepreneurs.

In August 2026 the government approved land and tailor-made incentives for two data-centre projects: 200 acres at Jagnadhapuram near Visakhapatnam, to be allotted at a 25% discount on the APIIC cost for a Rs 58,743 crore, 486 MW project, and 433.30 acres at Makavaripalem in Anakapalli district at the fixed APIIC price, The New Indian Express reported.
APIIC's revenue, profit and staff numbers were not found in the official pages we checked.

detail: AIC was set up in 2002 by the General Insurance Corporation of India, NABARD and the four public sector general insurers to run crop insurance. The Department of Financial Services reported in January 2026 that it crossed Rs 10,000 crore in gross premium in 2025-26.

detail: The government announced a new South Coast Railway zone headquartered at Visakhapatnam in February 2019. Railways are run as a departmental undertaking of the Ministry of Railways: budget-funded, with no share capital and no legal identity of their own.

No zone-level revenue, profit or staff figures have been published; Indian Railways' accounts are consolidated nationally.

records.summary: The state's bus corporation, created under a 1950 Act of Parliament, running more than 11,000 buses from 129 depots. It lost about Rs 1,567 crore in 2023-24 on provisional figures. On 9 July 2026 the government denied reports that it was privatising APSRTC.
detail: APSRTC is a statutory corporation under the Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950. It traces its origins to June 1932, when it began as a wing of the Nizam State Railway, and says it runs from 129 depots and 423 bus stations, connecting 14,123 villages.

CARE Ratings' March 2025 rationale reports provisional figures of Rs 7,175.71 crore in total operating income and a loss after tax of Rs 1,566.76 crore for 2023-24, after a loss of Rs 1,770.80 crore in 2022-23, and a fleet of 11,216 buses. Its organisation chart listed 47,687 staff on 1 July 2024.

On 9 July 2026 the state's Special Chief Secretary (Transport) dismissed reports of APSRTC's privatisation as false, saying the induction of electric buses under the Centre's PM e-Bus Sewa scheme 'does not involve the transfer of RTC assets or services to private entities', The Hindu reported.

The yard delivered INS Nipun, the second Nistar-class diving support vessel, to the Navy on 30 July 2026, and the Navy commissioned it on 31 August 2026. The Ministry of Defence said it was 'indigenously designed and constructed by Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam'.

records.summary: The state company that owns the 2,400 MW Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah thermal power station at Krishnapatnam. In a report tabled on 6 March 2026 the CAG named it the source of 98% of the losses of Andhra Pradesh's loss-making state enterprises, with a Rs 1,227.55 crore loss and its net worth wiped out.
detail: APPDCL was formed in 2006 to build and run the Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah Thermal Power Station, three 800 MW supercritical coal units at Krishnapatnam, and sells its power to the state's distribution companies.

The CAG's compliance audit of Andhra Pradesh state public sector enterprises (Report No. 7 of 2025), tabled in the legislature on 6 March 2026, found that of Rs 1,251.63 crore lost by five state enterprises, '98.07 per cent amounting to ₹1,227.55 crore was contributed by one power sector SPSE i.e., Andhra Pradesh Power Development Company Limited'.

On its latest finalised accounts (2021-22), the CAG lists APPDCL's paid-up capital at Rs 2,068.28 crore, long-term borrowing at Rs 16,155.38 crore, accumulated losses at Rs 3,863.65 crore and net worth at Rs (-)1,795.37 crore. The same report counts 21 inactive Andhra Pradesh state enterprises that have 'effectively ceased to carry out their operations or are under liquidation process'.

records.name: Bihar State Financial Corporation (BSFC)
records.summary: BSFC is a state-level development financial institution established in 1954 under the State Financial Corporations Act, 1951 to finance small and medium industrial units. The Bihar government holds 51.32% and SIDBI 48.43% of its Rs 77.84 crore paid-up capital. It has done no fresh lending since 1990-91 and survives on recovery, rentals and deposits, with its Bihar-Jharkhand bifurcation still pending.

records.administrative: Government of Bihar
detail: BSFC's official about page states it was established in 1954 under the SFCs Act, 1951 as a state-level development financial institution to provide medium and long term credit to small and medium industrial units, headquartered at Vittya Nigam Bhawan, Frazer Road, Patna (source: bsfc.co.in/about).

Its official financial page gives authorised capital Rs 100 crore and paid-up capital Rs 77.84 crore with State Govt 51.32% and SIDBI 48.43%; it states IDBI/SIDBI dues are fully settled with nil outstanding, a State Govt loan of Rs 228.47 crore, cumulative disbursement of Rs 438.49 crore to 7,223 units, recovery of Rs 870 crore as on 01.06.2021, and 2,267 units in the loan portfolio as on 01.04.2024 (source: bsfc.co.in/financial).

The same official page states fresh financing stopped in 1990-91 after SIDBI stopped refinance, recovery is via sale of mortgaged assets under Section 29 of the SFCs Act, OTS-2018 realised Rs 41 crore, and the audited 31.03.2018 balance sheet showed liabilities Rs 595.63 crore against assets Rs 208.72 crore; bifurcation between Bihar and Jharkhand (65.03:34.97) is pending after an inconclusive secretary-level meeting on 14.12.2018 (source: bsfc.co.in/financial).
records.caveats: No 2025 or 2026 official development (results, CAG finding, revival order) could be confirmed from opened pages; the most recent official data point is the 01.04.2024 loan-portfolio figure. Latest revenue/profit and employee figures are not published on the pages opened, so financials and employees are null. Administrative department not stated on opened pages.

records.name: East Central Railway (ECR)
records.summary: East Central Railway is a railway zone of Indian Railways under the Ministry of Railways. It is headquartered at Hajipur, Vaishali district, Bihar, and became operational on 1 October 2002. Its network is reported at about 9,518 track km and fully electrified as of 31 March 2025.

records.administrative: Ministry of Railways
records.legal_form: Railway zone under the Ministry of Railways
records.established: 2002: operational from 1 October 2002, carved from Eastern and North Eastern Railways
detail: ECR's official introduction page states the zone is headquartered at Hajipur (Bihar), became fully operational on 1 October 2002, was carved out of parts of the Eastern Railway and North Eastern Railway zones, and comprises five divisions: Danapur, Dhanbad, Pt Deen Dayal Upadhyaya, Sonpur and Samastipur (source: ecr.indianrailways.gov.in introduction page). The division-wise mapping (Sonpur and Samastipur from N.E. Railway; Danapur, Dhanbad and Pt Deen Dayal Upadhyaya from Eastern Railway) is stated on the Wikipedia page (source: Wikipedia East Central Railway zone page).

As of 31 March 2025 the zone is reported to operate 9,518.196 track km and 4,399.897 route km across Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh and to be fully electrified; Hajipur is the district headquarters of Vaishali, about 25 km by road from Patna (source: secondary compilation, Wikipedia East Central Railway zone page, which cites the ECR official site). The official introduction page likewise reports over 4,400 route km, more than 9,500 track km, four states, and 100% electrification of broad-gauge routes.

FY2024-25 station figures compiled on the same page put Patna Junction first (passenger revenue about Rs 816.11 crore, footfall about 5.93 crore), followed by Danapur and Muzaffarpur Junction (source: secondary compilation; an official zone-level earnings release for 2025-26 was not opened).

In August 2026 it announced the induction of 549 new buses including electric buses under the PM e-Bus Sewa scheme, taking the fleet from about 960 to 1,526. records.name: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL)
records.summary: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited is a Navratna defence shipyard under the Ministry of Defence, headquartered at Dockyard Road, Mumbai. The President of India held 84.83% as on 31.03.2025. Its most recent official development is the keel-laying of the fourth Fast Patrol Vessel (Y-16504) and plate-cutting of the seventh vessel (Y-16507) for the Indian Coast Guard on 06 Apr 2026 at Mumbai.
records.state_link: Central enterprise headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra (Dockyard Road, Mumbai-400010)

records.established: 1934 as a private limited company; acquired by the Government of India in 1960
records.financials: FY2024-25 (annual report): revenue from operations Rs 11,431.88 crore; profit before tax Rs 3,109.20 crore; profit after tax Rs 2,324.88 crore
detail: MDL is described in its FY2024-25 annual report as the 'Ship & Submarine Builders to the Nation', operating shipbuilding facilities at Mumbai and Nhava under the Ministry of Defence, and the only Indian shipyard to have built both destroyers and conventional submarines for the Indian Navy (source: MDL Annual Report FY2024-25).

DPE lists Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd. among Navratna CPSEs in its January 2026 schedule-wise list; MDL states it was conferred Navratna status by DPE in June 2024, the first government-owned shipyard and third defence PSU to receive it (sources: DPE CPSE list January 2026; MDL Annual Report FY2024-25).

For FY2024-25 MDL reported record revenue of Rs 11,431.88 crore (up 20.76% from Rs 9,466.58 crore in FY2023-24) and record PAT of Rs 2,324.88 crore (up from Rs 1,845.43 crore), with net worth Rs 7,180.84 crore (source: MDL Annual Report FY2024-25 / directors report).

On 06 Apr 2026 MDL conducted the keel-laying of the fourth Fast Patrol Vessel Y-16504 and plate-cutting of the seventh vessel Y-16507 of the 14-vessel Indian Coast Guard programme at Mumbai, presided over by DIG Rajesh S. Gandhe (source: MDL official website news).
records.caveats: Employee count not confirmed in pages opened, left null. FY2025-26 audited figures (revenue Rs 12,839.64 cr, PAT Rs 2,435.77 cr) appear in later filings but FY2024-25 annual report used as stable audited source; April 2025 OFS proposal for up to 4.83% not treated as on-the-block.
